name: Christopher Wylie

summary.text: Christopher Wylie is a Canadian data consultant who worked as research director at SCL and became the principal public source for the March 2018 reporting on Cambridge Analytica's use of Facebook data. He gave oral evidence to the UK DCMS Committee on 27 March 2018 and supplied documents the committee later published, and testified before the US Senate Judiciary Committee on 16 May 2018. His statements about AggregateIQ, Palantir employees, SCL's 2014 contacts with Lukoil and Black Cube were disputed by those companies.

facts.claim: Wylie gave oral evidence to the DCMS Committee on 27 March 2018 and gave the committee access to a large number of documents, which the committee later published as written evidence and background papers.
facts.quote: the Chair noted that Wylie had given the Committee access to a large number of documents that he has, and the Committee planned to review them before publishing some.

facts.claim: Wylie told the DCMS Committee he 'absolutely' believed AggregateIQ drew on Cambridge Analytica's databases for its Vote Leave work, and said he had helped found AggregateIQ while research director at SCL; AggregateIQ responded that it had never been part of Cambridge Analytica and had never signed a contract with the company.
facts.quote: Wylie on Tuesday told the media committee of the British parliament that he "absolutely" believed Canadian consultant AggregateIQ drew on Cambridge Analytica's databases

sources.title: 'They Don't Care': Whistleblower Says Cambridge Analytica Aims To Undermine Democracy
AggregateIQ statement on Wylie testimony

facts.claim: Wylie told UK lawmakers that senior Palantir employees worked on the Facebook profile data acquired by Cambridge Analytica and 'helped build the models we were working on', while saying there was no official contract between the companies; Palantir first said it had never had a relationship with Cambridge Analytica, then said an employee had engaged 'in an entirely personal capacity' with people associated with the firm.
facts.quote: He also said Palantir staff "helped build the models we were working on." He described it as not an official contract between Palantir and Cambridge Analytica.

sources.title: Palantir worked with Cambridge Analytica on the Facebook data: whistleblower
Palantir confirms a staff link with Cambridge Analytica

facts.claim: In supplementary written evidence to the DCMS Committee, Wylie stated that after a request for information from Lukoil in spring 2014, Cambridge Analytica discussed its disinformation experience and microtargeting work, that documents sent to Lukoil created by Alexander Nix included sections on 'Rumour campaigns' and voter 'inoculation' in Nigeria, and that this was documented in correspondence and slide decks in the committee's possession.
facts.quote: documents sent to Lukoil created by Alexander Nix includes sections on "Rumour campaigns" and on voter "inoculation" in Nigeria.

facts.claim: Wylie testified before the full Senate Judiciary Committee on 16 May 2018 at a hearing titled 'Cambridge Analytica and the Future of Data Privacy', chaired by Senator Grassley, alongside Eitan Hersh and Mark Jamison.
facts.quote: The Senate Judiciary Committee's own page lists it as a full committee hearing at 10:00am in Dirksen Room 226, presided over by Chairman Grassley, with Wylie, Eitan Hersh, and Mark Jamison as witnesses.

sources.publisher: US Senate Committee on the Judiciary
sources.title: Cambridge Analytica and the Future of Data Privacy

facts.claim: At the Senate Judiciary hearing Wylie said that during his time at Cambridge Analytica employees of SCL Group were in contact with Lukoil, that Steve Bannon engaged SCL to build 'an arsenal of informational weapons', and that the company offered services to discourage voting among targeted groups; he did not provide specific evidence of voter suppression campaigns taking place in the US.
facts.quote: Wylie told lawmakers that during his time at Cambridge Analytica, employees of its parent corporation SCL Group were in contact with Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil company.

sources.title: Whistleblower: Cambridge Analytica aimed to trigger paranoia and racial biases
Whistleblower: Cambridge Analytica Aimed To Trigger Paranoia And Racial Biases

facts.claim: Wylie told the DCMS Committee in March 2018 that Cambridge Analytica had used the Israeli private intelligence firm Black Cube on a 2015 Nigeria project to obtain Muhammadu Buhari's medical records and private emails; Black Cube called the testimony a 'flagrant lie' and said it had never worked for SCL or Cambridge Analytica or operated in Nigeria, and Cambridge Analytica said it had never worked with or been in contact with Black Cube.
facts.quote: Wylie told UK lawmakers in March 2018 that Cambridge Analytica "utilized the services of an Israeli private intelligence firm, Black Cube,". He said Black Cube on the Nigeria project was engaged to hack the now-president Buhari to get access to his medical records and private emails.

openQuestions: The Times of Israel reported that Wylie retracted the Black Cube allegation in US Senate testimony in May 2018; the Senate transcript should be checked for his exact words.
Wylie's written statement to the Senate Judiciary Committee (linked from the committee page) was not opened; the account of his testimony is from AP/NPR coverage.
The Lukoil slide decks Wylie supplied to the DCMS Committee were not located among the published background papers.
